title: fix(layer): improve exported layer resolution to avoid blurry output
body:
## Description

Text layers that were rotated, for example by 12°, had a noticeably lower quality and only rendered at full quality when rotated exactly 0° or 90°. This PR resolves that issue.

The actual fix was made in the `pro_image_editor` package, so this PR simply bumps the package version to include that fix.


**Related Issue:** Closes #4059

title: fix(audio): allow choosing audio start time for community sounds
body:
## Description

Fixes a bug where users could not select a custom audio start time for community sounds in the video editor.

The root cause was that `AudioTimingCubit` required the remaining audio (from the chosen start offset to the end of the source) to be at least as long as the video's maximum duration (6.3 s). This made most of the waveform non-draggable — any start position that left less than 6.3 s of tail audio was rejected, effectively locking the start time to the very beginning.

The fix introduces `minRemainingAudioSecs = 0.5` so users can scroll the waveform all the way to within 0.5 s of the audio's end. The visible segment indicator on the timeline is also clamped to the actual playable clip length so it shrinks visually as the user approaches the end of the source audio.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes

- **`AudioTimingCubit`** — added `static const double minRemainingAudioSecs = 0.5`; `_scrollableAudioSecs` and `initialize()` now use this constant instead of implicitly requiring a full-video-length tail
- **`VideoAudioEditorTimingScreen`** — `_VideoDurationTimeline` now clamps the segment indicator width so it reflects the actual playable clip rather than always showing a full-width bar near the end of the waveform
- **`AudioEditorSelectionOverlay`** — replaced inline `Duration(milliseconds: 300)` with `VineTheme.defaultAnimationDuration`
- **`AudioSelectionBottomSheet`** — added `isLoading` state while audio loads, preventing interaction with a not-yet-ready audio service

## Testing

- Updated `audio_timing_cubit_test.dart` — all 32 tests pass
- `flutter analyze` reports no issues

Closes #4753

title: feat(clips): allow saving own videos to clip library
body:
## Description
 

Previously the "Add to clips" action in the share sheet was only available for classic Vine videos. This PR extends the import pipeline so users can also save their own uploaded divine videos into the local clip library for use in the video editor.

### What changed

**`VideoClipImportService` (renamed from `ClassicVineClipImportService`)**
- Generalised to accept any `VideoEvent`, not just classic Vines.
- Added a `VideoMetadataReader` typedef (`Future<VideoMetadata> Function(EditorVideo)`) injected via constructor (default: `ProVideoEditor.instance.getMetadata`).
- Added `_resolveAspectRatio`: prefers the Nostr event's `dim` tag; if absent, probes the downloaded file via `ProVideoEditor.getMetadata` (handles `rotation == 90 / 270` by swapping width/height). Exceptions are caught, logged with `Log.warning`, and gracefully fall back to vertical.
- Clip ID scheme distinguishes own videos (`own_video_<eventId>_<ts>`) from classic Vines (`classic_vine_<vineId>_<ts>`).

**`VideoClipImportProvider` (renamed from `ClassicVineClipImportProvider`)**
- Wires the generalised service into the Riverpod provider graph.

**`ShareSheetBloc` / events / state / reportable sites**
- `ShareSheetAddClassicVineToClipsRequested` → `ShareSheetAddVideoToClipsRequested`
- `ShareSheetClassicVineClipImportResult` → `ShareSheetVideoClipImportResult`
- Import service field updated accordingly.

**`share_action_button.dart`**
- Visibility gate changed from `video.isOriginalVine && !kIsWeb` to `(video.isOriginalVine || isOwnContent) && !kIsWeb`, enabling the action for own content.
- Wires the renamed provider and event.

Closes #4622

### Tests

- `video_clip_import_service_test.dart` – all 8 tests pass:

title: fix(notifications): preserve normalized payload on foreground local notification taps (#4728)
body:
## Description

Foreground FCM banners displayed a local notification via `sendLocal()` **without a tap payload**, so tapping a foreground-generated notification did nothing — the shared router (#4727) had no context to route with. This PR closes the foreground payload gap **and** the local-notification cold-start gap that #4728's acceptance criteria call out.

### Payload production (foreground)
- **Extract `localNotificationTapPayload()`** (`notification_helpers.dart`) as the single source of truth for the local-notification tap payload shape — `referencedEventId`, `eventId`, `notificationType` (from the FCM wire `type`), `senderPubkey`. The background/system-push handler (`main.dart`) and the foreground handler now **both build it**.
- **`sendLocal()`** gains an optional `payload` param, threaded to the plugin's `show(payload:)`.
- **`handleForegroundMessage()`** attaches the normalized payload, so foreground taps — including follow/mention, which carry no `referencedEventId` — route through the same contract as background/system-push taps.

### Payload consumption on cold start (new)
`divine-push-service` sends **data-only** FCM messages (`notification: None`, `android: None`; an APNS `aps.alert` is synthesized only for iOS). So on **Android every push is rendered locally** by `flutter_local_notifications`, and a tap that launches the app from a **terminated** state arrives via `getNotificationAppLaunchDetails()` — **not** `getInitialMessage()` (which only covers OS-rendered iOS pushes). That launch path was never consulted, so Android terminated-app taps were silently dropped even with a valid payload attached.
- **`NotificationService.takeLaunchNotificationTap()`** consults `getNotificationAppLaunchDetails()` once at startup (next to `getInitialMessage`) and routes any launch payload through the shared `_routeNotificationTap`.
- **`_parseTapPayload`** extracted so the live-tap and cold-start paths share one parser.

### Review hardening
- **`NotificationPayloadKeys`** centralizes the payload field names previously hand-mirrored across the writer and the two readers; `localNotificationTapPayload` is now derived from `parseFcmPayload`, sharing its empty-string normalization rather than re-deriving it.
- **Plugin injection seam** (`debugConfigurePlugin`, `@visibleForTesting`) so `sendLocal(payload:) → show(payload:)` forwarding and the cold-start path are unit-tested — the prior round-trip test bypassed both.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4728 (parent epic #4200). Builds on #4727 (merged in #4736).

## Out of Scope
- **#4730** — `referencedDTag` owned-video attribution safety.
- **#4731** — duplicate push rendering. Note: #4760 (#4731) edits the same `_firebaseMessagingBackgroundHandler` this PR touches — whichever merges first, the other rebases.
- The routing contract itself (shipped in #4727); this PR makes the foreground path *produce* and the cold-start path *consume* the payload the contract relies on.

## Verification
- `flutter analyze lib test` → **No issues found**
- `flutter test` notifications surface (`test/services/*notification*`, `test/notifications/`, `test/main_notification_tap_routing_test.dart`) → **295 pass**, incl. new `sendLocal` payload-forwarding, `takeLaunchNotificationTap` cold-start (routable / not-launched / no-details), and empty-string normalization.
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` → clean

title: Bug: keep publish flow alive while expired-session recovery is in progress on iOS
body:
## Summary
On iPhone, an expired Divine OAuth session can interrupt an in-progress publish flow and route the user into login/session recovery before silent refresh has definitively failed.

In the reported incident, the clip upload and publish succeeded, but the app still routed into `/welcome/login-options` during session recovery. That makes the app feel like it logged the user out mid-publish.

## Incident evidence
- Silent refresh attempt starts at `2026-05-22 08:02:09` (`tryRefreshExpiredSession: attempting silent refresh`).
- Router redirects to `/welcome/login-options` at the same time, while auth state is still reported as authenticated.
- Publish later completes successfully at `2026-05-22 08:02:17`.

## Why this matters
Even when the publish succeeds, the user experiences the flow as a forced logout during creation. If refresh fails for real, the app still needs to preserve enough local state for a clean resume.

## Suspected code areas
- `mobile/lib/services/auth_service.dart` around `tryRefreshExpiredSession()` and `_tryRefreshOAuthSession()`
- `mobile/lib/screens/settings/settings_screen.dart` session-expired handling
- `mobile/lib/widgets/profile/profile_header_widget.dart` session-expired handling
- Router/auth redirect interactions during refresh

## Fix direction
- Treat silent refresh as atomic from the UI's perspective.
- Do not navigate away from the active flow until refresh definitively fails.
- Preserve publish state while refresh is in flight.
- If refresh fails, resume from a durable interrupted-publish state after re-auth.

## Acceptance criteria
- Successful silent refresh keeps the user in the active publish flow.
- Failed silent refresh surfaces a resumable interrupted-publish path instead of losing local context.
- Add regression coverage for publish + app resume + expired session on iOS-oriented flows.

Parent epic: to be linked after creation.

title: fix(e2e): move emulator launch and stack setup into scripts
body:
Closes #4762

## Summary

The E2E skill had too many shell recipes that agents had to copy by hand.
This change moves the repeatable setup, emulator, and local-stack steps into scripts and mise tasks.
It also keeps the auth harness aligned with localized copy so copy edits do not break the happy path again.

## What Changed

The dev harness now owns the deterministic setup work that used to live in prose.
Agents can run the named tasks instead of reconstructing Android SDK, emulator, Docker, and log-diagnostic commands from `SKILL.md`.

- Added `local_stack/android_sdk.sh` to find the Android SDK in standard Linux and macOS locations.
- Added emulator tasks for normal, headless, and wipe launches.
- Defaulted emulator selection to the first available AVD and kept `ANDROID_AVD_HOME` override-friendly.
- Gated Linux X11 / XWayland display probing so macOS launches use the native emulator path.
- Moved local stack startup into `local_stack/up.sh` so `local_up`, `local_up_cached`, and `local_reset` share one service list.
- Made `local_setup` safe to run repeatedly, including fail-loud handling for non-empty `master.key/` directories.
- Made `local_reset` depend on `local_setup` before wiping and restarting the stack.
- Added native Android test XML excerpt printing when patrol reports `Total: 0` with a non-zero exit.
- Trimmed `.claude/skills/e2e-test/SKILL.md` from 256 lines to 179 lines.
- Updated auth E2E helpers to use generated English l10n values instead of hardcoded auth labels.
- Added a reset-password helper that fills both password fields before submitting.
- Squashed the branch to one conventional commit so the semantic commit gate can pass.

## Testing

The script checks cover the review-sensitive shell behavior without launching a full emulator.
The reset-password helper is covered by a widget regression test, and the l10n lookup guard prevents the helper from drifting back to hardcoded auth copy.

- [x] `bash local_stack/test_android_scripts.sh`
- [x] `bash -n local_stack/android_sdk.sh local_stack/emulator.sh local_stack/profile.sh local_stack/setup.sh local_stack/up.sh local_stack/test_android_scripts.sh`
- [x] `flutter test test/integration_test_helpers/navigation_helpers_l10n_test.dart test/screens/auth/reset_password_test.dart`
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test`
- [x] `git diff --cached --check`
- [ ] `mise tasks deps e2e_test` -> `e2e_test -> local_up -> local_setup`
- [ ] `mise run emulator` launches AVD with no `ANDROID_HOME` exported
- [ ] `bash local_stack/setup.sh` runs silently on a clean working tree
- [ ] Full auth E2E journey against the local Docker stack

## Risks

The app binary is not affected.
The risk is limited to local developer and agent harness behavior.

- Emulator launch behavior depends on the installed Android SDK and available AVDs.
- The full E2E journey still depends on a healthy local Docker stack and emulator storage state.

title: feat: add frame count option to one-touch capture

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### What would you like?

Add a frame count option to the one-touch = one-frame stop motion feature so each capture can automatically create multiple frames (e.g., 2 frames per tap instead of only 1).

### How would this be useful for you?

This would speed up animation workflows by reducing the need to duplicate frames manually. It also makes timing more consistent for users who commonly animate on twos or use longer default exposures per pose.

### When would you use this?

When creating stop motion animations where each pose should last multiple frames by default, such as animating on twos.

### Anything else?

Currently clips can be shortened easily, but extending them requires duplicating frames manually.
